conceptZh: 扭蛋小怪獸先把「山」和「石」疊反了，發現後輕輕一撞翻回正確位置，旁邊的玩具火山滾下一顆岩石。
creativeAngle: 先蓋錯上下，再一撞修正。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy, locked frontal camera. Setting: a soft salmon-pink backdrop with a sandy floor; the glyph is solid slate-gray 岩, 山 above 石. A round fuzzy creature bursts from a gachapon capsule at left; a small toy volcano stands at the far right. The Traditional Chinese glyph 岩 stays centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the capsule pops and the creature bounces out, proudly dropping a heavy 石 block on top and the 山 peaks beneath it, upside-down; the first 岩 is spoken as it tosses the first block. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): it blinks at the wrong stack, shrugs, and bumps the pile once with its belly; the two pieces swap and slot into 山 over 石 with a clack; the second 岩 is spoken at the clack. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): the volcano rumbles gently, puffs a pink smoke ring and a sparkly gray rock rolls down to the floor with a thud; 岩石 is spoken as the rock lands. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 岩 is perfectly still and unobstructed; the creature hops onto the rock, rides it a few inches and bounces off; the glyph is still. Voice: a gentle off-screen narrator in Taiwanese Mandarin pronounces exactly 「岩、岩、岩石」 with Zhuyin ㄧㄢˊ、ㄧㄢˊ、ㄧㄢˊ ㄕˊ, slowly and distinctly, tones clear. Timing: first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 2.5s, the word at about 4.4s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only thuds and a soft volcano rumble, no music. The single glyph is the only on-screen text; the vocabulary stays audio-only with no subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing.

conceptZh: 浣熊助手花生和積木小隊搶一顆綁著繩子的大灰岩石，兩邊拔河拔到臉紅腳滑，繩子「啪」地彈開，兩邊跌坐在地，大岩石震成碎塊，落成「岩」字。
object: a big round slate-gray toy boulder with a thick rope looped around its middle, sitting center stage between Peanut the raccoon and a marching squad of building bricks
morph: the tug-of-war rope snaps back, the boulder shudders and bursts into slate-gray chunks: three jagged peaks tumble up and stack as 山 on top, while the wide flat slab, the slanted sliver and the square hollow chunk settle beneath as 石, completing 岩
creativeAngle: 上一版是小怪獸疊錯字再撞回去，動作小、笑點弱。這版改成大人小孩都秒懂的拔河：花生和積木小隊各拉繩子一端搶大岩石，花生的高塔在他敬錯禮時先倒一次（角色性格），積木小隊在最緊張時整隊歪倒，繩子彈開兩邊跌坐，大岩石被震碎落成「山」上「石」下的「岩」。「岩石」一詞說出時花生正舉起一顆小灰石頭敬禮，聲音與畫面完全對應。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D cartoon comedy with a locked frontal camera. Setting: a pale cream backdrop with a flat sandy-tan floor, nothing busy behind. The Traditional Chinese glyph 岩 (山 stacked on top of 石) is formed from solid slate-gray boulder chunks; when finished it is centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with clean margins, and it is the only text on screen. Lead: Peanut, a cartoon raccoon sidekick with a striped tail, big round eyes and a tiny yellow bandana, who always carries a wobbling tower of things too tall for him and salutes at the wrong moment. Supporting cast: a squad of five chunky interlocking building bricks in red, blue and yellow that march in step and stack into a tower. Prop: one big round slate-gray toy boulder sitting center stage with a thick rope looped around its middle, two loose rope ends trailing left and right. Moment one, want it (0.0-1.6s): Peanut shuffles in from the left balancing a teetering tower of small grey pebbles, spots the boulder, gasps with sparkly eyes, and snaps a proud salute; the pebble tower immediately topples over his head and scatters behind him. He grabs the left rope end anyway. The brick squad marches in from the right, clicks itself into a tower and clamps onto the right rope end. The first 岩 is spoken at about 0.7s as Peanut grabs the rope. Moment two, try and miss (1.6-3.6s): tug-of-war. Both sides lean further and further back, heels skidding in the sand, Peanut's cheeks puffing red, the brick tower wobbling and leaning at a crazy angle; the rope stretches thinner and thinner like licorice while the boulder rocks and rumbles. A frozen beat: everyone strains, eyes squeezed shut. Moment three, the big crash (3.6-5.0s): the rope snaps back with a cartoon TWANG; Peanut flies backwards onto his bottom at the left edge with a soft bonk and the brick squad tumbles apart onto its backs at the right edge. The shaken boulder shudders and bursts into slate-gray chunks: three jagged peaks bounce up and lock together as 山 on top, and the wide flat slab, the slanted sliver and the square hollow chunk settle beneath as 石, all clacking into the finished 岩 with a short puff of dust. The second 岩 is spoken at about 4.3s exactly as the last chunk clacks into place. Moment four, the payoff (5.0-8.0s): the glyph 岩 stays perfectly still, unobstructed and fully readable for the final three seconds. At the far left Peanut sits up dizzy with a wobbly grin, picks up one small grey rock from his scattered pile, hoists it over his head with both paws and then salutes with one paw so the rock wobbles on his head; the word 岩石 is spoken at about 5.6s exactly as he lifts the little rock. The bricks at the far right sit up, wobble, and tip over again at the very end. Nobody touches the strokes. Voice: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly these syllables, slowly and distinctly with clear tones, Taiwan standard readings, no erhua: 「岩、岩、岩石」 (ㄧㄢˊ、ㄧㄢˊ、ㄧㄢˊ ㄕˊ). Short pauses between utterances; stop after 岩石, no repeats, no extra speech, no translation. Only soft cartoon sounds beneath the voice: sand skids, a stretchy rope creak, a gentle twang, rock clacks, no music. Bright, clean colors, no neon, no white blowout, no dark grading. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter, no flashing effects.
